rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and identify critical pairs while keeping the run reasonably short. The low starting organic fraction retains early compounds, and the high endpoint reduces the risk of missing strongly retained compounds.

Test temperature selectivity against injection 1 while keeping the gradient unchanged. Higher temperature may separate the early cluster and shorten retention without the time penalty of a shallower gradient.

Retain the favorable high-temperature selectivity and use a shallower gradient to improve the sole unresolved pair. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, leaving room to reach full resolution without a time penalty.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so shift the starting organic fraction to test selectivity instead. This higher start should also shorten retention while preserving useful retention of the first peak.
